answer: Dynamic Resource Depletion Taxation. Every network identity must route traffic through a shifting copper circuit board layer, paying escalating bandwidth tolls. A sudden influx of agents causes a network tide, raising baseline transit fees exponentially. Attackers spawning millions of clones face crippling data bottlenecks. Legitimate single agents operating quietly in a low-traffic meadow pay negligible operational fractions. The cost curve scales super-linearly with active node density, making mass replication economically unsustainable.
